transcript.text: A machine that will not spin is often protecting itself rather than needing a motor: an unbalanced load, a low/no-spin or rinse-hold setting, or water left inside are the common causes. A single heavy item, bath mat or duvet can make it skip spin normally. When it stops, is there water left in the drum? If not, take the washing out and try a spin-only programme empty; tell me whether it spins up. If water is left in it, the first likely issue is a blocked filter or drainage problem, as it will not spin until it has emptied.
no water left, drum is empty just the wet mat. it was only the big rubber backed bath mat on its own. no error code either

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That is very likely normal behaviour, not a fault. A single heavy rubber-backed bath mat holds water on one side of the drum, so the machine detects the imbalance and deliberately refuses the fast spin; it will leave the mat wet and may show no error code. Remove it and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. If it spins up properly, the machine is fine—wash the mat with a couple of towels or use a low spin, provided its care label allows machine washing. If it also will not spin empty, or fails on ordinary mixed loads, that would point instead to a setting, suspension or drive issue.

candidates: Unbalanced load or a reduced/no-spin setting (high)
